what_happened: A job ("Require a stated check method for subjective-quality outcomes") was dispatched on the branch tip at the same moment another job's pull request landed. Landing rebuilt the branch on the merged commit, so the new job's base commit was no longer on the branch. The job passed its checks and verification, costing about $7.50, then went stale and could not land. The same thing happened again at 11:51 UTC. This is not a content conflict on governed files. The base commit itself was rewritten. The the person running Athena did not retry by hand and reported it for Athena's loop.
cause: Dispatch and landing are not coordinated. A job takes the branch tip as its base without checking that a landing is in progress. Landing rewrites the branch history instead of adding to it, so any job started during that window has a base that no longer exists. Athena has no path to move verified work onto the new base, and staleness shows up only when the job tries to land. Passed work is therefore discarded because of timing, not because of any fault in the work.
prevention: Two changes together would cover the class. (1) Dispatch must not start a job while a landing is rebuilding the branch. It should take a lock or wait, and record the base commit at dispatch. (2) A job that goes stale, whether from rewritten history or from a governed-file conflict, should be rebased onto the new main automatically. Only the cheap checks and a re-verification should be rerun, not the producer. Where rebasing is not possible, serialize jobs that could touch the same base.
proposed_request: When a job goes stale because main moved under it (another landing rewrote the branch, or a governed-file conflict), Athena must carry the verified work onto the new base instead of discarding it. Outcome: (1) Dispatch does not start a job while a landing is rebuilding the branch, and each job records the base commit it started from. (2) When a job's base is no longer on the branch at landing time, Athena rebases the verified change onto current main, reruns the checks and verification, and lands it if they pass. It does not rerun the producer. (3) If the rebase conflicts, the job is reported as stale with the conflicting files named, and is not marked failed. Acceptance: a test starts a job, lands another job's change so the branch is rebuilt, and shows the first job lands after the automatic rebase without a producer rerun. A second test shows a conflicting rebase ends as stale with the files named. Dispatch during a landing waits instead of starting.
